newsitem.title: DENMARK: FOCUS - Audio exports buoy Denmark's Bang & Olufsen.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Audio exports buoy Denmark's Bang & Olufsen.

text.p: Boosted by solid growth in key export markets and higher sales of telephones, upmarket Danish audio, video and television manufacturer Bang & Olufsen (B&O) on Wednesday reported bumper half-year profits and forecast almost 20 percent higher results for full year 1996/97.
The company posted pre-tax and minorities profits of 174 million crowns ($27.6 million) on 1.550 billion crown turnover, 16 percent up on the first half of the previous year.
B&O said that its audio/video division, accounting for 90 percent of all sales, logged turnover of 1.405 billion crowns.

It said sales grew the most in the United States, with 52 percent, while in the relatively untried Italian market they climbed 31 percent and British sales rose 26 percent compared to the same 1995/96 period -- all measured in Danish crowns.
B&O said its biggest market remained neighbouring Germany but first-half growth there had been only five percent. The Danish home market logged a 14 percent increase.
B&O, 25 percent owned by Netherlands-based Philips Electronics NV, makes sleek audio products for the exclusive, luxury goods market as well as producing telephones and medical equipment.

It said that its telecoms division had the biggest growth rate, at 52 percent, boosted by increased sales of mobile, cordless and fixed telephones and telecommunications, while its technology division, which produces medical equipment, reported 44 percent growth.
B&O posted 32 percent better first half 1996/97 pre-tax profits and forecast a whole year result nearly 20 percent up on 1995/96.
"We expect turnover to increase by more than 10 percent with the pre-tax and minorities result to be around 325 million crowns for full year 1996/97," B&O said in a statement.
Its main targets for 1996/97 and 1997/98 were an annual rise in earnings of a least 15 percent, with turnover growing at least five percent on an annual basis.
"B&O expects to achieve all its targets during the present year," it said.
B&O's whole year 1995/96 pre-tax and minorities result was 272 million crowns on 2.717 billion crown turnover.
It said it planned to launch a new audio/video product and speaker in unspecified markets in April in keeping with its declared aim of introducing a new product concept every year.
